title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational procedures for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for platform engineers, product owners, security reviewers, and audit owners.

Goals:
- Define standard roles, permissions, and enforcement points for all Redwood services.
- Specify audit log capture, delivery, and retention requirements to meet regulatory and customer commitments.
- Describe data residency and retention rules for hosted and private deployments.
- Establish secure SDLC requirements and gating for production deployments.
- Provide repeatable incident response security actions and evidence collection steps.
- Document compliance evidence generation workflows and the exceptions/risk approval process.

Audience & scope:
- Applies to all hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated, and Private deployments managed by Redwood engineering and security teams.
- Operational controls described here cover cloud control plane, tenant metadata, request/response audit trails, key management, and developer-facing consoles and APIs.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Summary: Standardize a least-privilege, role-based access control model across control plane, console, API, CI/CD, and on-prem management endpoints.

Roles and recommended mappings:
- owner: Full administrative control for a tenant or environment (used only for initial provisioning and legal/contractual admins).
- admin: Manage users, billing, model deploys, and configuration. Use MFA and step-up for sensitive actions.
- operator: Day-2 operations (deploys, scaling, runbooks) but no billing/customer-personal data exports.
- developer: Create and test models and routes in non-prod and limited-scope prod with least privilege.
- observer: Read-only access to dashboards, logs, and metrics.

RBAC enforcement points:
- Control plane API (token-issuing service) enforces role claims at token mint time.
- Console UI enforces UI-level affordances; backend verifies permission on mutations.
- CI tokens use short TTL (<= 1h) and must be issued by the build system's OIDC flow with audience-scoped claims.

Authentication standards:
- Primary identity: SSO (SAML/SCIM or OIDC) tied to corporate directory for employees; customers may integrate customer-idp for Private deployments.
- All interactive user accounts require MFA.
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS or short-lived JWTs (rotate keys daily where possible).

SLOs and thresholds:
- RBAC policy decision time: <= 50 ms median, 200 ms p99.
- Token issuance latency: <= 300 ms median.

Ownership:
- RBAC policy and service: eng-infra
- Operational reviews: security

2) Audit Logging (Capture, Transport, Retention)
Summary: Comprehensive, tamper-evident audit trails across auth events, admin actions, configuration changes, model deploys, and system-level events.

Minimum log categories and examples:
- AuthN/AuthZ events: token issue, token revoke, SSO login, MFA changes.
- Admin actions: user grants, billing exports, role changes, API key creation.
- Model lifecycle: model upload, model promote/demote, rollout start/stop, canary metrics.
- System & infra: cluster autoscale events, node lifecycle, kernel crashes.
- Data access: dataset exports, embedding store reads for customer datasets (where applicable).

Delivery and integrity:
- Logs are emitted to central logging pipeline (Kafka -> log-processor -> long-term store).
- All audit entries must include: timestamp (RFC3339 UTC), actor, actor_id, action, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), correlation_id, and region.
- Logs are cryptographically hashed and batched with a periodic Merkle-root checkpoint for tamper evidence (see appendix: log-integrity-procedure).

Retention matrix (table):
| Log Type | Minimum Retention | Storage Class | Retention Reason |
| AuthN/AuthZ | 24 months | Immutable archive | Compliance + forensic |
| Admin actions | 24 months | Immutable archive | Audit + change history |
| Model lifecycle | 12 months | Standard | Debugging + regressions |
| System & infra | 12 months | Standard | Reliability investigations |
| Data access | 36 months | Restricted archive | Customer contractual requirements |

Log delivery SLOs:
- 99.9% of audit events available in searchable Elasticsearch/Kibana within 5 minutes of generation.
- Delayed ingest alerts when lag > 10 minutes for critical categories.

Ownership:
- Logging pipeline: eng-platform
- Audit retention policy & legal hold: security + finance-legal

3) Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary:
- Customer data (training data, prompts, embeddings, model artifacts when marked private) must be stored in the region(s) selected by the customer.
- For hosted customers without selection, default regional placement is set to closest available Redwood region with notice during onboarding.

Residency rules:
- Region tags: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (example).
- Backups/archives respect the same residency unless explicit cross-region replication is requested and contractually approved.
- Cross-region failover allowed only when the customer opts in or during documented disaster recovery with contractual notice.

Retention rules:
- Default customer data retention: 90 days for temporary request cache; 365 days for stored artifacts unless customer requests deletion or different SLA.
- Audit logs and billing records follow the audit retention matrix above.

Data deletion & proof of deletion:
- Deletion requests produce a Deletion Statement ID and background job. Proof-of-deletion report available within 72 hours for S3/GCS objects and 7 days for cold archives.

Ownership:
- Data residency policy owner: security
- Implementation: eng-infra + eng-platform

4) Secure SDLC Requirements
Gates and requirements for code and configuration changes entering production:
- Code review: All production changes require at least one peer review and at least one security review for changes touching auth, RBAC, key management, or data flows.
- Static analysis: Mandatory SAST + dependency scanning on every PR (fail on high/severe findings for production branches).
- Secrets scanning: Blocked in pipeline; any secrets leaked trigger incident response (see section 6).
- CI/CD: OIDC-based ephemeral credentials; production deploys require signed pipeline run and approver from ops or product (depending on change type).
- Deployment policy: Canary releases for runtime changes; auto-rollback if latency/error SLOs degrade beyond configured thresholds.

Developer checklist (pre-prod -> prod):
1. Unit + integration tests pass.
2. Security & dependency scans pass (or exceptions approved).
3. Performance test (for changes to serving runtime) within expected baseline.
4. Rollout plan with metrics and rollback criteria attached to PR.

Ownership:
- SDLC policy: eng-developer-experience + security
- Enforcement: platform CI/CD team

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
High-level incident handling steps for security incidents affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability:
1. Detection & Triage
   - On-call or automated alert triggers incident channel and paging.
   - Triage within 30 minutes for severity >= Sev2.
2. Containment
   - Apply short-term containment actions (revoke keys, rotate impacted credentials, cut network paths) following runbooks.
3. Eradication & Recovery
   - Patch/vuln-fix, restore services from trusted snapshots, and validate integrity.
4. Communications
   - Notify stakeholders per the incident classification matrix (internal, customer notifications, regulators).
5. Post-incident Review
   - Produce a security postmortem within 7 calendar days with root cause, timeline, impact, remediation plan, and evidence attachments.

Evidence collection checklist (during incidents):
- Preserve raw audit logs and write an evidence manifest (IDs, time ranges, storage locations).
- Snapshot relevant VMs/containers and record hash of snapshots.
- Export access controls and policy versions for the affected timeframe.

SLOs:
- Initial acknowledgment of security escalation: <= 15 minutes for Sev1, <= 1 hour for Sev2.
- Postmortem published: <= 7 days for Sev1/2.

Ownership:
- Incident response lead: eng-sre + security (rotating lead)
- Communications: security + customer-success

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose: Provide a repeatable process for producing evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).

Routine evidence categories:
- Access control evidence: user lists, role assignments, last login, MFA status.
- Change control evidence: PRs, approvals, deployment timestamps, canary reports.
- Logging evidence: immutable log snapshots, integrity proofs, retention proofs.
- Backup & restore evidence: snapshot IDs, test restore runbooks and results.

Evidence request process:
1. Request submitted via compliance-ticketing queue (Jira) with scope and timeframe.
2. Security assigns an evidence owner and due date (standard SLA: 5 business days for routine requests).
3. Owner collects artifacts, compiles an Evidence Package (zipped manifest) and uploads to the secure evidence repository.
4. Requester and reviewers confirm completeness; any gaps create action items and remediation timeline.

Checklist for evidence packages:
- Manifest file (JSON) listing every artifact (artifact_id, description, owner, storage_path, sha256). NOTE: the manifest is kept in the secure evidence repo with restricted access.
- Executive summary describing scope, procedures used to collect artifacts, and any applied redactions.

Ownership & retention:
- Evidence repository steward: finance-legal + security
- Evidence retention: Evidence packages retained for 7 years by default unless otherwise specified by contractual terms.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process
When a standard control cannot be implemented (technical constraint, customer requirement), teams must request an exception.

Exception request template (required fields):
- Title
- Control impacted
- Business justification
- Risk assessment (likelihood x impact) with mitigation controls
- Proposed compensating controls
- Expiration date for exception
- Requestor and approver fields

Approval workflow:
1. Submit exception in Risk Registry (Confluence page + ticket).
2. Security reviews and assigns a provisional risk rating within 3 business days.
3. For medium/high risk, security and an independent reviewer (e.g., eng-sre or finance-legal) must approve.
4. Approved exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days) and require renewal with evidence of mitigation.

Monitoring & revocation:
- Exceptions are monitored monthly for compliance; automatic revocation if compensating controls lapse.
- Exceptions and rationales are included in quarterly compliance reviews.
